notes:
Account summary
- Vertex AI Tools is an AI tooling vendor (agent workflow + eval/monitoring) looking at a technology partnership where Redwood is a selectable inference backend inside their product. They also want guidance on how to position the combined story for marketplace-driven procurement (AWS first, GCP later).

What they said (call notes / snippets)
- "We’re getting pulled into enterprise deals where the buyer already has AWS Marketplace as the procurement path." They want a clean story: buyer buys Vertex + inference in one motion OR buyer buys inference via marketplace and Vertex plugs in.
- "Our customers complain about inference being the flaky part" — they want Redwood’s reliability / fallback narrative and operational controls to be part of the joint value prop.
- Interested in a co-branded quickstart: Vertex workflow template + Redwood API key + a baseline eval pack (latency/cost/quality) to prove day-1 value.

Integration angles discussed
- Product integration: Vertex UI can configure Redwood endpoints (Hosted) and later support Dedicated endpoints for predictable throughput. They asked about:
  - Streaming support + tool/function calling (needed for agent flows)
  - Structured outputs / JSON mode patterns (they have validators)
  - Multi-model routing: choose model by cost/latency tier; automatic fallback if capacity constrained
  - Per-route metrics to feed back into Vertex observability dashboards (token/cost/latency)
- Commercial integration: they are exploring whether Redwood SKUs can align with their packaging.
  - Option A: customer brings their own Redwood account (recommended to avoid reseller complexity).
  - Option B: joint marketplace procurement guidance (private offers for enterprise).
  - They asked if Redwood can provide an 'integration partner' SKU/credit program for their sandbox environments.

Marketplace + co-marketing requests
- Co-marketing: webinar + short case study + a benchmark blog post (latency/cost). They want Redwood to provide performance numbers but are okay with directional + caveats (hardware/model/version pinned).
- Marketplace listing cross-linking: they want to mention Redwood as a supported inference backend in their AWS listing, and want Redwood to mention Vertex in 'Works with' / partner section (if allowed by partner rules).
- Assets: requested 1-2 diagrams: reference architecture (Vertex app -> Redwood API -> model runtime) + onboarding flow (subscription -> org provisioning -> API key -> first call).

Requirements (technical / security)
- Security posture: they’re okay with public SOC2 statement + security overview, but for enterprise joint deals they need:
  - audit logging coverage (API key events, org/admin changes, entitlement/provisioning events)
  - retention controls / data handling summary they can reuse in their own questionnaires
- Deployment: they expect most early customers to use Hosted API; Dedicated is the upsell for predictable throughput. Private/on-prem is 'nice to have' but not required for initial partner launch.

Buying signals / deal context
- Not a direct buyer yet; more like a partner that can drive influenced pipeline. They claim ~15 active enterprise evaluations where inference provider selection is still open.
- Potential direct spend: they may run a small internal Dedicated cluster for demos (hence estimated ARR range), but main upside is sourced/influenced deals.

Open questions
- Who owns L1 support in a joint integration? Need crisp escalation path (Vertex -> Redwood support) and agreed boundaries.
- Can we publish co-marketing content without implying joint warranty/endorsement? Needs PMM/legal review.
- Clarify whether Redwood can share benchmark screenshots/console visuals publicly (must match marketplace-approved language).

Internal follow-ups
- Markus to draft an integration checklist (auth patterns, rate limiting, retries, idempotency, telemetry fields) and propose a joint quickstart repo outline.
- Stephanie to align with Partnerships on whether we can include partner mention in marketplace listing copy and what approval steps are needed.
- If we proceed: create a lightweight partner enablement pack (FAQs + security pointers + marketplace procurement steps) for Vertex SEs.
